The '''Kubaz''' or '''Kubazian''' were an insectivorous [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kubindi/Legends|Kubindi]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Although relatively new to the [[galactic community]] at the time of the institution of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the species was already ubiquitous throughout the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] during the [[Great Galactic War]] and the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Kubaz_AA.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Kubaz.]]
A bipedal [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species of [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]], the Kubaz were distinctive for their short, prehensile facial snouts which were used for reaching [[Insect/Legends|insects]] within their hives.<ref name="UAA" /> Having adapted to their sun-scorched, vegetation-deprived world, the Kubaz learned to survive off their world's native insect population. Filled with two rows of teeth for gnashing their food, the Kubaz trunk also functioned as a highly sensitive nose.<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> Green-black skinned, Kubaz had short bristly hair growing from their heads and they stood upon two-toed feet. Having evolved on their homeworld of [[Kubindi/Legends|Kubindi]], a planet which orbited a [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Star/Legends|star]], the Kubaz were highly sensitive to red wavelengths. When traveling to planets with a red or yellow star, the Kubaz were forced to don protective eye wear to avoid damaging their sensitive eyes.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==

The Kubazi society was based on a family-oriented clan structure which dwelt in underground nests. Ruled by a queen, each clan took the name of their queen they were descended from. Their extended families included all descendants of a living Kubaz and their spouses. Families overlaped, with every married Kubaz belonging to both their original and their spouse's family. Marriage was the traditional method of strengthening long-term inter-family peace. While their families are large and strong, they are not clans in the usual sense. Clans trace their descent from a common ancestor, while Kubaz families trace their descent strictly to their eldest member.<ref name=":0">{{Journal|10|A Free-Trader's Guide to the Planets}}</ref> 

Family elders were highly regarded and were the focus of the care and attention of the entire family. Elders watch over the family in a state of semi-retirement. They advise the family, but for the most part they reign without ruling. Ordinary family business was handled by the first-born (the First), with the advice of the next two eldest siblings (the Second and Third). This group was collectively known as [[the Three]]. If one of the Three were to die, then the eldest child of that individual inherits the Third position while the other two surviving members advanced in position. The three eldest offspring of the Three stayed in the family compound and married younger members of another family, while younger members married older members of other families.<ref name=":0" /> 

While family membership was lifelong and dual, individual Kubaz were theoretically supposed to hold primary allegiance to the family they resided with regardless of genetic connection. The war between personal preference and dual family pressures had led to familial conflicts of interest spanning countless generations. Entire genres of Kubaz literature and theater revolved around the theme of familial conflict. Despite this, the cross-attachment of families led to an overall peace in Kubaz society by keeping most families related to each other and thus removing the incentive for large scale conflict. The balance of power amongst families naturally realigned every few decades as they lost significant influence every time an elder died. When this happened, the Three unevenly divided their inheritance. The First received one third of their elder's assets, the Second one quarter, and the Third one fifth. The remaining assets were scattered among the rest of the family. The new elder would then set up shop as the head of new families.<ref name=":0" />       

Developing a non-verbal language of hand gestures which indicated their intentions, Kubaz were able to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], though with a strong nasally accent. When interacting with other species, some Kubaz would share certain hand signals with non-Kubaz in order to ease communications. Touching the nose, head, or shoulders could indicate intent, direction, and number.

[[File:kubazchef.png|thumb|right|275px|A Kubaz chef without protective eye wear.]]
The Kubaz developed a high culture independent of other galactic influences. Obsessed with tact and decorum, the Kubaz place a high emphasis on the family unit and proper courtesies, displaying truthfulness to a fault. Valuing art and literature with such vigor as to sometimes practice smuggling of great works, the Kubaz did not find such pursuits to be wrong or unlawful.<ref name="UAA" /> Arts such as cuisine, sculpting, crafts, and sciences were of special interest to the Kubaz, with experts in such fields being granted great societal support. They were renowned for their unusual high cuisine which was centered around the fine preparation of insect meals. Their insect cuisine became Kubindi's largest export, with Kubaz chefs having been sought after by Kubaz high cuisine enthusiasts such as [[Beldorion|Beldorian]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]<ref>''[[Planet of Twilight|The Planet of Twilight]]''</ref> and [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Spitar P'ton]]. When Admiral P'ton made contact with the Kubaz for the first time, he quickly came to appreciate their advanced culture, art, theater, and cuisine. He hired a staff of Kubaz chefs and introduced Kubaz cuisine to the highest circles of Imperial society. The Empire's high regard for Kubaz culture spared Kubindi from the overt and rapacious attention other non-human species faced.<ref name=":0" /> Due to their habitual diet on Kubindi, the Kubaz had poor relations with other sentient insectile species such as the [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosians]].<ref name="The Long Arm of the Hutt">{{FFG|story=The Long Arm of the Hutt|book=Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Beginner Game|text=''Star Wars: Edge of the Empire'' Beginner Game}}</ref>

==History==
Descended from insectivorous [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]], the Kubaz were native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kubindi/Legends|Kubindi]], a world which suffered from intense solar flares from their planet's sun. The flares were so extreme much of Kubindi was scorched rock devoid of above-ground vegetation. As the Kubaz delved underground in search of insects to harvest, rival clans began raiding each others' insect farms. Erupting into the open conflict known as the [[Hive Wars]], the bloody civil war was eventually resolved through the scientific advancements in the field of ''[[insecticulture]]''. Altering the genetics of their insects to reproduce more rapidly and efficiently, the Kubaz also implemented a system of color-coding each clan's food supply differently so as to identify which bugs belong to which clan.<ref name="UAA" />

As war became a distant memory the Kubaz began to make great strides in the fields of science and spacecraft construction. Building [[Starship/Legends|starships]] which were restricted to their own local [[Star system/Legends|star system]], the Kubaz were able to colonize three of the eleven worlds which orbited their local [[Blue giant/Legends|blue giant]], [[Ku'Bakai]]. As colonies erupted on [[Ku'Bakai 11]], [[Ku'Bakai 6|6]] and [[Ku'Bakai 8|8]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] discovered the world and the Kubaz were able to move out of their home system by securing passage from paid transports. Not long after the Kubaz began to explore neighboring systems did they encounter the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]]. Seeing them for insectoids and ignoring their sentience, the Kubaz were in danger of violating the rights of several insectoid species before the Republic intervened. Discouraging the race from developing [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] technology, the Kubaz were forced to rely on visitors to take them to and from Kubindi.<ref name="UAA" />

[[File:DelvaRacine.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Fashion designer [[Delva Racine/Legends|Delva Racine]] developed an entire collection based on Kubaz appearance.]]
Enveloped in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] during the last decades of the Republic, the Kubaz were free from the oversight of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] for many years and became slightly more widespread, appearing as poachers on some worlds where insectoids were frequent. As the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] ground on in the greater galaxy, the Kubaz began to develop their own hyperdrive technology but were quickly sabotaged by Imperial agents when the Galactic Empire came to power. The Imperial propaganda machine quickly churned out false leads pointing to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] as the true perpetrators of the attacks to discourage the race from looking to join their cause. Despite Imperial attempts some saw through the lies and joined the Alliance as spies or agents of espionage. Others joined the Empire and worked in crowded cities and ports, reporting to the local Imperial garrisons on the goings-on of local taverns and other breeding grounds for dissension and rebellion. During this era, the Kubaz established a colony on [[Doornik-319]], which they named Morning's Bell.<ref name="Before the Storm">''[[Before the Storm]]''</ref>

Following the fall of the Empire, the Kubaz began talks with the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] but were invaded by the [[Yuuzhan Vong empire]] in [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]]. Despite being caught unawares, many Kubaz were able to [[Battle of Kubindi|evacuate]] their home system thanks to the efforts of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Kyp Durron]] and his [[Kyp's Dozen|starfighter group]]. As the Yuuzhan Vong were responsible for exterminating nearly all life on Kubindi, the Kubaz who remained on the planet died of starvation. As the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] saw its conclusion and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] took to restoring the galaxy, the surviving Kubaz returned to their homeworld to begin the rebuilding process. Their species greatly diminished, the Kubaz were aided by the [[Hutt Empire]] and as of [[127 ABY]] remained a part of the [[Hutt dependencies]].<ref name="NEGAS" />

==Kubaz in the galaxy==
Thanks to their high culinary culture, Kubaz [[chef/Legends|chefs]] were legendary. The [[Unidentified Kubaz chef|best known Kubaz chef]] in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was assigned to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], while the [[Tavvar Va'ran|second best]] graced the [[Manarai]] restaurant, cooking for the [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] elite.<ref>{{WEGCite|story=A Very Special Meal|book=Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook}}</ref>

[[File:Garindan.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Garindan/Legends|Garindan]], a male Kubaz.]]
Many Kubaz abroad were [[Spy/Legends|spies]] sent to other worlds by their respective hives to learn about other worlds' politics, cultures, and cuisine&mdash;to the Kubaz, this would be native insects. Their taste for insects sometimes caused problems. Not recognizing [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] beings as anything other than a food source, Kubaz would sometimes illegally purchase the bodies and body parts of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] insectoid [[Species/Legends|species]]. Spying, however, was not the only path Kubaz took, but rather they were a highly educated species that appreciated art, music, and literature. They were social beings that focused on mannerism and refinement and embraced traditions and history of their kind, so placing them under one occupation would not be representative of the species.<ref name="UAA" /> A population of Kubaz was present on the planet [[Garnib]].<ref name="PGV1">''[[Planets of the Galaxy, Volume One]]''</ref>

Despite their finer points, some Kubaz were involved in the criminal underworld. A number of Kubaz joined the violent [[Black Heth]] criminal gang on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in the time prior to the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]].<ref name="SW:OW">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref> Later, during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], one Kubaz by the name of [[Garindan/Legends|Garindan]], a member of [[Zabin Hive]], led [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] to the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] while [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] tried to smuggle them off [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="SWE4">{{Film|IV}}</ref> His close relative, [[Udin]], was a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], who later captured Luke Skywalker for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], but accidentally turned him over to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].

While [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] Kubaz were exceedingly rare, one known member of the race was recorded as fighting in the [[New Sith Wars]] as a member of the [[Novitiate]] [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. Named [[Glenk]], the Sith was actually a spy for the [[Daimanate]] Sith and was quick to betray his assumed Master [[Odion]] at the [[Massacre on Skarpos|Battle of Skarpos]].<ref name="Knight Errant: Escape 3">[[Knight Errant: Escape 3|''Knight Errant: Escape'' 3]]</ref> No members of the Kubaz species were ever recorded as being inducted into the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="UAA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Kubaz first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].
